raw_model_output.headline: Supreme Court Judge Alleges Misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Judge
raw_model_output.body:
Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma [c69]. Mehta sent three letters in August 2026 to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant [c69].

Mehta alleged cases were abruptly moved to Sharma's bench without valid cause [c72]. He claimed Sharma held a meeting on a working day to designate favored lawyers as senior advocates [c73]. Mehta also cited a complaint claiming Sharma appointed personal associates to Lok Adalat positions in Jaipur and Ajmer [c81].

In addition, Mehta criticized a plan for a 100-room guest house tower as a waste of public funds [c74]. He urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court immediately [c77].

Chief Justice Surya Kant requested a formal response from Sharma [c76]. Kant said allegations against sitting judges must follow institutional channels rather than public debate [c71].

Sharma became Acting Chief Justice in September 2025 and retires on September 26 [c70] [c75]. He was first appointed a judge in November 2016 [c78].

parsed_body:
Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma. Mehta sent three letters in August 2026 to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.

Mehta alleged cases were abruptly moved to Sharma's bench without valid cause. He claimed Sharma held a meeting on a working day to designate favored lawyers as senior advocates. Mehta also cited a complaint claiming Sharma appointed personal associates to Lok Adalat positions in Jaipur and Ajmer.

In addition, Mehta criticized a plan for a 100-room guest house tower as a waste of public funds. He urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court immediately.

Chief Justice Surya Kant requested a formal response from Sharma. Kant said allegations against sitting judges must follow institutional channels rather than public debate.

Sharma became Acting Chief Justice in September 2025 and retires on September 26. He was first appointed a judge in November 2016.

claims_available.text: Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta sent three letters in August 2026 to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant alleging misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma.
Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma was appointed Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court in September 2025.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that allegations against a sitting judge must be handled through established institutional mechanisms and not determined in the public domain.
Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged that cases were abruptly withdrawn and transferred to Acting Chief Justice Sharma's bench without justifiable cause.
Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged that Acting Chief Justice Sharma organized a full court meeting on a working day to designate favored lawyers as senior advocates.
Justice Sandeep Mehta criticized a plan for a multi-storied guest house tower with nearly 100 rooms for the Rajasthan High Court as a waste of public funds.
Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma is scheduled to retire on September 26.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant confirmed he has requested a formal response from Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma regarding the allegations.
Justice Sandeep Mehta urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court to Rajasthan with immediate effect.
Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma was appointed a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in November 2016 and transferred to the Patna High Court in 2022.
In March 2023, the Supreme Court collegium headed by DY Chandrachud declined Justice Sharma's request to return to Rajasthan and transferred him to the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
In May 2025, the Supreme Court collegium recommended Justice Sharma's return to the Rajasthan High Court.
Justice Sandeep Mehta highlighted an advocate's complaint alleging Justice Sharma used his authority to appoint personal associates to permanent Lok Adalat positions in Jaipur and Ajmer.
